_note: Real ML Kit line output for a two-column card whose telephone block puts a small FAX caption beside the number it labels, captured 2026-09-03. The caption arrived as its own box.
_anonymised: Boxes are exactly as ML Kit reported them, converted from the captured centre-y and height. Company names, the person's name, the email and every telephone number are replaced by strings of the same shape - same word counts, character classes, lengths and OCR damage, including the stray space before the '@' and the leading 'O' the recogniser read off a handset glyph. Certification marks are left as printed: they are public standard names and belong to nobody.
_source: Samsung SM-G736B, ML Kit text-recognition, Latin. Line angles between -2.8 and +0.9 degrees.
_layout: Left column: logo, website, then a stack of certification marks. Right column: two company names, the role and the person, then the telephone block. The FAX caption sits to the LEFT of its own number rather than above it.
_why_it_matters: The FAX caption is 1.5625 line heights from its number and the two are one field - they must merge. card_three_column.json has a name and a title 1.545 heights apart that must split. The must-merge gap is the wider of the two, so no single MAX_GAP satisfies both: this pair is what falsifies the threshold rather than merely leaving it untested.
